blockMcqs.question: Which model is a teaching reference, not a running implementation?
blockMcqs.explanation: OSI is a reference framework; TCP/IP is the model the real internet implements.

blockMcqs.question: Why does layering let you swap Wi-Fi for Ethernet without changing HTTP?
options: HTTP and Wi-Fi share the same header
Each layer only talks to the layers directly above and below it
Wi-Fi and Ethernet use the same MAC address
HTTP runs at the Physical layer
blockMcqs.explanation: Layer isolation means upper layers don't care how the lower layer moves bits — only the interface contract matters.

blockMcqs.question: Which OSI layer is responsible for routing packets using IP addresses?
blockMcqs.explanation: Layer 3 (Network) handles routing — it reads IP addresses to decide where packets go next.

blockMcqs.question: Which TCP/IP layer corresponds to OSI layers 5, 6, and 7?
blockMcqs.explanation: TCP/IP's Application layer merges OSI's Session, Presentation, and Application layers (5-7).

blockMcqs.question: What is a PDU?
options: A unit of data at a specific layer with its header
A protocol used only at layer 3
The maximum transmission speed on a link
blockMcqs.explanation: PDU (Protocol Data Unit) is the named chunk of data at each layer — segment, packet, frame, or bit.

blockMcqs.question: What does the Data Link layer strip during de-encapsulation?
blockMcqs.explanation: Each layer removes only its own header. Data Link strips the frame header/trailer and passes the IP packet upward.

blockMcqs.question: At which OSI layer does DNS operate?
blockMcqs.explanation: DNS is an application-layer protocol — it runs at OSI Layer 7 (Application).

blockMcqs.question: A switch forwards traffic using MAC addresses. Which OSI layer is this?
blockMcqs.explanation: MAC addresses belong to Layer 2 (Data Link), so a switch that reads them operates at Layer 2.

blockMcqs.question: Which statement about encapsulation is correct?
options: The internet runs the OSI model
Headers are added going down and stripped going up
blockMcqs.explanation: Encapsulation adds headers at each layer as data descends; de-encapsulation strips them as data ascends on the receiver side.
